task: Reduce canonical root npm test from 1688.9 seconds to under 300 seconds through safe resource-aware concurrency and redundant-work elimination without weakening assurance.
outcome: After running the same-material build and npm test, the terminal reports every completeness-checked full-suite member PASS and a total duration below 300 seconds; three clean temporary-clone runs produce the same result with no leaked children or hidden retry.
facts: The current B-9812 base has 45 canonical root members; the previously measured B-cdf6 descendant had 46 because it additionally included audit-scan-bin-token.
Most members use unique mkdtemp roots and can run concurrently, while repository-scanning and wrapper-authority tests need explicit repository-read or exclusive resource declarations.
The acceptance suite currently creates 24 production cohort cases because runCohort is invoked twice; each case repeats the same 26-command CLI lifecycle.
The real CLI sentinel can stay in proofstory-pre-review-check-smoke while frozen cohort mutation and threshold checks run from one generated cohort in process.

Intent-hardening uses repeated CLI calls through one helper and needs differential assertion inventory before any batching; incremental-context has two deterministic masks plus a 20-iteration identical-mask burn-in that can be separated only with a retained mutation-killing deterministic case.
The existing run-all-smokes runner retries TIMEOUT and allowlisted FAIL results, so canonical mode requires no-retry as a hard default rather than an optional flag.
constraints: Preserve current deterministic assertions, mutation bites, dist and CLI black-box sentinels, and gate semantics.
Unknown or conflicting shared resources run serially; isolated temporary roots are required for concurrent writers.
An initial FAIL or TIMEOUT remains terminal for the canonical full suite.
Membership completeness must fail on omissions, duplicates, or unexpected skips.
Performance acceptance uses three clean temporary-clone runs after same-material builds and records machine-readable timings.
